name: print the axis and let the scale be chosen
one_line: An axis printed with no numbers on it, filled in by whoever collects the data once they know what range they are in.
how: Print the axis and never the scale: the numbers up the side get written after the counting, which is the first moment they can be known. Choose something to count that matters to nobody — how often the house telephone rings, when the light comes on in the building opposite — because a count with an expected result has something to betray. Once a day at the same hour, five days, one point each. Print a second lane parallel to the first over the same span: the world above, this house below. Last line, a real question with no single answer: join the points or do not, and write in one line why you decided that.

knobs.effect: Printed, the numbers are decided before anything is counted and half the sheet ends up empty or off the top; left blank, the range is chosen once the data are in, and that is the decision the form exists for.
One lane is a series; two parallel lanes over the same span — the world and the house, the street and the kitchen — produce coincidences nobody arranged, and the second lane costs one printed rule.

Joining them asserts that something continuous happened between two readings, which is sometimes false; asking for the decision and its reason is the only place on a printed sheet where that gets asked at all.

Left blank, a missing reading reads as an omission by whoever was counting; marked with a question mark, the notation Priestley used where a date was not known, it becomes a way of writing «not known» that is not an empty space.

where_the_work_is: In what gets counted. It has to be countable in under a minute, available at the same hour every day, and of no importance to anybody, or days two to five never happen.
breaks: A form in two parts across five days, and nothing makes the later days arrive; a sheet with one point on it is not a fifth of a result. Printed axes scan back well and pencil dots on them do not, so ask for crosses. Two lanes with a few labels are the one graphic thing in this chapter a display can carry whole.
